interview.answer: The algorithm that resolves conflicting declarations by importance, origin, layer, specificity and source order.
A weight assigned to a selector that determines which declaration wins when origins and layers are equal.
As (a,b,c): a for IDs, b for classes/attributes/pseudo-classes, c for elements/pseudo-elements.

interview.q: What is the specificity of an inline style?
interview.answer: Higher than any selector, represented as (1,0,0,0) in the four-part model.
It raises a declaration to the important origin, overriding normal specificity.
It breaks the cascade and makes overrides hard, leading to specificity wars.
Named layers created with @layer that let you control precedence without specificity battles.
It declares a cascade layer and assigns rules to it, with later layers winning over earlier ones.

interview.q: What is the benefit of cascade layers?
interview.answer: They make third-party and base styles predictable by ordering layers explicitly.
A feature query that applies styles only if the browser supports a given property or value.
Ship a baseline that works everywhere, then enhance behind a feature query for capable browsers.
A query that styles an element based on its container's dimensions, enabling reusable components.

interview.q: How do you establish a container for container queries?
interview.answer: Apply container-type: inline-size to the parent, which creates a query context for descendants.

interview.q: Why name a container in CSS?
interview.answer: So container queries can target it explicitly instead of the nearest container.
The ability to nest selectors inside one another, reducing repetition.
It represents the parent selector in nested rules.
Selecting a parent based on its children, enabling previously impossible styling.

interview.q: When is subgrid useful for card layouts?
interview.answer: When nested components need to align to the parent grid's tracks.
It matches any of a list of selectors with the specificity of the most specific argument.
It matches any of a list of selectors but contributes zero specificity.

interview.q: How can color-mix() derive a hover colour?
interview.answer: Mix a brand colour with white or black in a perceptual colour space.
It returns one of two values based on the user's colour scheme without a media query.

interview.q: How do you use the color() function for wide gamut?
interview.answer: Pass a colour space such as display-p3 to access colours outside sRGB.
A wide-gamut colour space with more vivid colours than sRGB.
A perceptually uniform colour space that makes gradients and palettes more predictable.
A perceptual colour space used for mixing and gradients.
It derives a new colour from an existing one by adjusting channels, such as oklch(from red l c h).
It balances the length of lines in a heading for a more even appearance.
It avoids orphans and improves line breaking in paragraphs.
It lets punctuation hang outside the text box for optical alignment.
It creates a drop cap by sizing the first letter to span multiple lines.
It snaps scroll positions to defined points for a controlled scrolling experience.
It defines the snapping behaviour on a scroll container, such as x mandatory.
It sets where an item snaps within the container, such as start or center.
It controls scroll chaining and pull-to-refresh behaviour.
It positions an element relative to an anchor element without JavaScript.
It links a positioned element to a named anchor.
It names an element as an anchor for positioning.
It limits a set of styles to a subtree, providing encapsulation without shadow DOM.

interview.q: What is the difference between @scope and shadow DOM?
interview.answer: @scope is a styling boundary; shadow DOM is a full encapsulation boundary including markup and events.
It lets form controls size to their content automatically.
It removes native styling from form controls so they can be fully customised.
It sets the accent colour of form controls such as checkboxes and radio buttons.
It sets the colour of the text input caret.
It controls whether text can be selected by the user.
